results.summary_before: This chip implements a Simon Says memory game where a sequence is stored in RAM and the player must repeat it using two input buttons. The design is tested with a Cocotb testbench that verifies programming, correct input, and error detection. External hardware such as switches and LEDs is suggested for manual testing.

results.summary_before: This project implements a hardware triangle rasterizer that renders filled triangles to a 256x256 viewport on a 640x480 VGA display. It uses the edge-equation method with incremental evaluation to avoid per-pixel multiplications, and triangles are loaded serially via an 8-bit input with a valid strobe. The design requires a VGA PMOD and monitor, and an external microcontroller to send triangle data. It is notable for its efficient hardware rasterization suitable for embedded graphics.

results.summary_before: This design implements a 32-bit iterative multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit with a 7x8-bit multiplier, intended for tiny ML accelerators. A controller FSM manages partial sums and bias alignment across four training phases or one inference phase. The design is verified with cocotb tests comparing against a reference model, and it requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout carrier. It is notable for its iterative architecture suitable for resource-constrained AI applications.
